digest.component_or_area: LLM workflow model selection and escalation
propositions: Pass-1 ladder entries are hardcoded to bare Anthropic model names, causing direct Anthropic resolution even when a non-Anthropic provider is configured for the workflow (split-brain at model_ladder[0] → cfg.model in batch runners)
Escalation via models_at_or_above() returns bare Anthropic ids with substring matching, causing a Bedrock-primary workflow to silently escalate to direct Anthropic rather than staying on Bedrock

Three separate code sites (production_batch_runner.py, code_review/batch_runner.py, workflow/runners.py) independently read model_ladder[0] without resolution, creating three separate split-brain instances

MODEL_LADDER serves dual roles—ordering escalation AND computing P8 context-window budget via substring match on bare names—so class-name entries would break the window-budget computation by failing the substring test

resolve_model_string already exists (delivered by f844) to map class names to provider-qualified models, and must be wired at config.resolve_model and all ladder-consuming sites, with lazy import in config.py to avoid a module-level cycle
workflow/runners.py:120 is a fourth consumer of model_ladder not previously in scope, performing the identical model_ladder[0] assignment without class resolution
